To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the A8V, D145E, and E134D HCM-cTnc mutants, but not WT, have a lower off-rate for Ca2+ in the presence of myofilaments and S1.

the increased Ca2+-sensitivity of HCM-cTNc mutants is potentiated by cross-bridges, that the Ca2+ off rates of these mutants are slower than that of the WT protein, and that this slower Ca2+ off rate can be directly correlated to the diastolic function impairment seen in patients with the A8V or D145E mutations.
the Ca2+ off rate is the major factor responsible for the increased Ca2+-affinity of HCM-cTNc mutants and that the effect is potentiated by strong cross-bridged.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms that underlie the increased Ca2+-sensitivity of HCM-calcium-binding protein (cTnC) mutations.
the molecular mechanisms that govern the Ca2+ sensitivity of the thin filament in the context of the myofilament,
the role of Ca2+ on the myofilaments in the regulation of cardiac contraction, with the ultimate goal of understanding the molecular mechanism of heart failure
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HCM-cTnc mutations, which have a higher Ca2+ affinity, are associated with a slower koff, a higher Ca2+-sensitive state and a lower ATPase activity.

the A8V, D145E, and E134D HCM-cTnc mutants are all capable of producing a diastolic dysfunction in vivo, but the A8V mutant is most likely to cause the greatest degree of diastolic dysfunction, followed by the D145E mutant

the HCM-causing mutations A8V and E134D have no effect on the myofilaments, while the HCM-causative mutations D145E and E180G increase the Ca2+ sensitivity of the contractile apparatus, but only in the presence of strong cross-bridging.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ca2+ dissociates more slowly from the HCM mutants than WT cTnC, resulting in a more potent Ca2+ sensitized state.

the HCM mutations A8V and E134D increase Ca2+ sensitivity of the myofilaments, while D145E increases both Ca2+ sensitivity and Ca2+ affinity, and the slower koff of A8V and DE145 may be the cause of diastolic dysfunction.
the Ca2+ off rate of the cTnCs is affected by the mutations and that the cross-bridges are able to potentiate these changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
strong cross-bridge interactions can modulate the Ca2+ binding properties of the cTnCs, and therefore the Ca2+ sensitivity of muscle contraction.
the cross-bridge is a major factor in the increased Ca2+-sensitivity of the HCM-cTnc mutants and that this effect is more pronounced in the A8V than D145E mutant.
the Ca2+ sensitivity of HCM-cTFs can be further increased by strong cross-bridging.
